question: A shopkeeper allows a 4% discount on his marked price. If the cost price of an article is ₹120 and he has to make a profit of 10%, then his marked price must be:
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

The relation between **Marked Price (MP)** and **Cost Price (CP)** is given by: **MP ÷ CP = (100 + Profit%) ÷ (100 − Discount%)**.

MP ÷ 120 = (100 + 10) ÷ (100 − 4)

MP ÷ 120 = 110 ÷ 96

MP = (110 × 120) ÷ 96

MP = 13200 ÷ 96 = 137.50

**∴ The correct answer is ₹137.50.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** CP = ₹120, Profit% = 10%, Discount% = 4%.

**Formulas:** SP = CP × (100 + P%) ÷ 100 | MP = (SP × 100) ÷ (100 − D%)

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c22c1cfe708f001dd5f03667b3d4a741bb440aea8e7c5626b7ea76595fcfdb3b.png] 

⇒ **Selling Price (SP)** = 120 × (110 ÷ 100) = 132

⇒ **Marked Price (MP)** × (100 − 4) ÷ 100 = 132

⇒ MP × 0.96 = 132

⇒ MP = 132 ÷ 0.96 = 137.50

**∴ The correct answer is ₹137.50.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Marked Price and Discount

The **Marked Price** is the price printed on the label, and **Discount** is always calculated on the MP to arrive at the **Selling Price**.

MP-CP Ratio Formula

The direct ratio **MP/CP = (100 + P%)/(100 - D%)** is the most efficient way to solve problems involving both discount and profit.
